scene_translation: When you inserted the old key into the lock, the door swung open with a faint sound. Inside was a small room, lit by a single candle. An old map was pinned to the wall, with a red circle drawn around one particular place. Opening the notebook, you found new writing in the hand of the woman in blue: 'テスト-san, next go to the old bridge at Suitengumae. Before dusk.'
grammar_note: 【〜てある】 Used here in 「貼ってある」and「描かれていた」— 〜てある describes a state resulting from a deliberate action, often implying someone arranged it intentionally. Compare: 「貼ってある」(someone put it there on purpose, it's still there) vs 「貼っている」(it is hanging). This hint of human intent adds to the mystery.

mystery_memo: Scene 6: Player has now entered the back room at the shrine and found a second message from the woman in blue — she names Suitengumae bridge as the next destination, urgently ('before dusk'), confirming she is actively guiding the player and knows their movements. The map on the wall may become a key item if the player chooses to take it. The notebook now contains two messages in her handwriting, both addressing テスト by name. The tobacconist from scene 3 (老人) is potentially connected — he directed the player toward the shrine area and seemed unsurprised; relationship: cautiously friendly. The notebook and key both originated from locker, suggesting the woman in blue placed them there specifically for テスト.
